claims.claim: Anthropic signed a landmark $11.6 billion, 7-year strategic cloud infrastructure agreement with Akamai Technologies.
claims.notes: Announced via joint press release and verified across Reuters.

claims.claim: The partnership focuses on enterprise CPU edge computing for autonomous agent execution, tool-calling routing, and local data residency.
claims.notes: Highlights expansion beyond centralized GPU clusters into distributed edge execution.

claims.claim: Akamai's distributed network spans over 4,000 global locations, providing sub-15ms edge inference routing and strict jurisdictional data isolation.
claims.notes: Addresses compliance under EU and Asian data sovereignty regulations.

claims.claim: Under this architecture, heavy reasoning runs on core GPU clusters, while agent memory, state management, and API tool interactions execute at the edge on Akamai CPUs.
claims.notes: Hybrid GPU-core and CPU-edge workload split.

claims.claim: This infrastructure agreement does not replace Anthropic's primary foundation training partnerships with AWS or Google Cloud; it serves inference and edge agent execution.
claims.notes: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: Clarify Akamai provides edge inference and agent execution, not primary pre-training clusters.

uncertainties: Phased rollout timeline begins in North America and Western Europe before global Asia-Pacific deployment.
